STAGE
PLAYS FOR SCHOOLS
Humorous and entertaining play giving children an opportunity to dress up as goodies and baddies in the wild, wild West. The new school teacher has to be escorted into town by stage coach.

FUN IN THE WILD, WILD WEST!
When the school teacher quits and leaves bring in a new one. There’s only one track Dakota Pass. The Chief of the Rap-dancin’ make some easy money. They hold-up the school teacher. Awesome! What happens their tribal elders...

INVOLVEMENT Projects on “Cultures” may be applicable in your school. Art and craft lessons to create cowboy suits, backdrops, bandanas, feathers, quivers, bows and arrows etc. will involve many students, plus follow up with discussion groups and written essays. Reports from internet forums can crystallise individual thinking on the subject. Building a pretend stage coach with rotating wheels, paper-mache horse heads, hessian horses, alfoil and lots of colours will keep many entertained. Plus, backdrops for the Saloon Bar scene and hills for the stage coach! Rapping lessons and accompanying dance music presents exciting opportunities for Poetry lessons. Whip cracking demonstrations may be possible, depending on location.
SONGS from the movie Calamity Jane “Black Hills of Dakota” “Careless With the Truth” “Secret Love” “The Deadwood Stage” “Background rap music for Rap-dancin’
Tribe”
Alternative songs appropriate to the generation may be used.
The Play is about 45 mins long. It may be lengthened by adding other songs. An Interval could be inserted between Acts.

There can be many non-speaking roles in the saloon bar; playing cards, leaning on the bar, hanging around the piano etc.
Although Calamity Jane is based in the wild, wild West, the Rap-dancin’ Tribe can be more a modern group of “Indians” who love to gather in a circle and play music, taking turns at Hip-Hop, Break Dance and Helicopter etc. This can involve more non-speaking roles drawing many more to attend the Play.

THE PLAY
ACT 1 Scene 1
Saloon Bar in the old West. Customers are anxiously waiting for Calamity Jane to arrive from Chicago and ride shotgun on the stage. Song: “Achy Breaky Heart” for line dancing in the Saloon.
ACT 1 Scene 2
Calamity and Rattlesnake arrive. Song: “Careless with the Truth”
ACT 1 Scene 3
Calamity and the others leave the Saloon to board the stage coach. ACT2 On the street outside the Saloon Bar. They board the stage coach and it starts to roll. Songs: “Windy City” and “Once I had a Secret Love”.
ACT 3 Somewhere on the edge of town. The school Rap-dancin’ Troup is enjoying the “moves” and discussing how they can “test” a new teacher before he comes anywhere near the school. Lots of Rap music.
ACT4 The stage coach arrives with Calamity, safely in Chicago. New teacher boards and they head back to Dakota. Song: “Deadwood Stage”. ACT5 The Ambush. The Rap-dancin’ Troup stop the stage coach to “test” the new school teacher. Song: “Black Hills of Dakota” plus Rap music. Teacher shows he can dance.
ACT6 Back in the Saloon Bar. All are waiting anxiously for the stage coach bringing the new school teacher. Song: Medley of songs from Calamity Jane plus Line Dancing and Rap.

ACT 1Scene1
A Saloon Bar in a pub in the old West. Choir can be extras on stage. Seated at tables are card playing cowboys and cowgirls. Cast includes Wild Bill Hickock, Army Lieutenant, Barman etc. As many as can fit on stage are Line Dancing and having fun as curtains open. Song and dancing ends and patrons whoop and cheer!
BARMAN: (Shouts) Hey, Wild Bill, when is Calamity gonna be here?
HICKOCK: Don’t know, Shabby. I wish she would hurry up. We need her to ride shotgun (pointing) on the stage coach out there. It’s about to leave.
1* COWBOY: Yep! We sure need some help to protect the stage coach. Every time it goes through Dakota Pass lately, that pesky Rap-dancin’ Troup stop the coach and annoy the passengers with their dancing. And they are some of our students from the school!
2" COWBOY: Last time we couldn’t get away for about 2 hours. They throw a blanket on the ground, hold up the stage coach, force the passengers to stand around ina circle... next thing they’re doing helicopters and doing break dancin’... the customers are not allowed to get back on the coach...
1 COWBOY:... and they put strings of beads around the passengers’ necks...
2"? COWBOY: And if you take the beads off, they make you rap dance.
LIEUTENANT: What?
BARMAN: Well, (holding up his beads) they ain’t gettin’ mine back... I had to do hip hop for about 10 mins so I could keep these beads! (All laugh!)

LIEUTENANT: (Walking up to the cowboy’s table) Look boys, let’s hope Calamity gets here soon. I wish she was here now.
BARMAN: Maybe we shouldn’t have fired the school teacher!
LIETENANT: Well, you caught him smoking in the classroom, didn’t you.
1* COWBOY: Yeh! He was real stressed out! Them kids kept makin’ him get down and dance... in the playground... like this! (Gets down and does some crazy rap-dancing)
2"? COWBOY: Well, Calamity will help us to bring the new school teacher into town. He’s a lot stricter! He’s from the Windy City, Chicago!
HICKOCK: Hey! That’s where Calamity is from too. Everything Calamity talks about is BIG! Especially her stories, hey boys! (High-fives 2" Cowboy)
BARMAN: Well I hope we can stop Calamity from tellin’ her yarns... just for 5 mins... so we can tell her about the school teacher problem that we got.
1* COWBOY: She'll probably tell that story about how she rounded up 500 buffaloes in the hills... all on her own...
2°? COWBOY:... and kraaled them in the Dakota Pass... (All laugh!)
HICKOCK: If Calamity don’t ride shotgun for us, the stage won’t be able to get through in time for school on Monday... (to audience)... and it would be real sad if we couldn’t have another new school teacher here by Monday... wouldn’t it! (Get reaction from audience. Song starts up again: “Achy Breaky Heart”... all line up and dance. Curtains Half Close to allow focus on Calamity Jane and Rattlesnake dancing their way through audience to the stage... Curtains Open fully as they enter stage and dance around with line dancers).
